0.0.n: A shortened まあ, used as a conversational filler before the main point.

0.2.n: Literally a castle’s central enclosure, 本丸 figuratively identifies the main objective here.

0.3.n: Marks 本丸 as the topic being discussed.

0.4.n: 付き means with; 給付付き describes a tax credit that includes a payment component.

0.5.n: Combines with 控除 to form 税額控除, a credit deducted from tax owed.

0.6.n: In 税額控除, this means a deduction from tax owed, not from taxable income.

0.7.n: Marks the content of what the speaker has been saying.

0.8.n: 申し上げる humbly means say; てまいりました politely presents the statement as continuing up to now.

1.0.n: Points back to the situation discussed earlier and directly modifies 状況.

1.1.n: Refers to the intended state of affairs described earlier.

1.2.n: Marks 状況 as what can be achieved with the potential expression 達成できる.

1.3.n: Combines with できる to mean can achieve or can be achieved.

1.4.n: After 達成, できる expresses possibility rather than saying the achievement has already happened.

1.5.n: Sets the endpoint: when the situation can be achieved.

1.6.n: Links the preceding until phrase to つなぎ, describing how long the stopgap is needed.

1.7.n: Names a temporary measure that bridges the gap until the intended solution becomes possible.

1.8.n: Marks つなぎ as the description the speaker has used.

1.9.n: The humble 申し上げる plus てまいりました presents a position repeatedly stated up to the present.

1.10.n: Introduces the reason for the statement that follows.

2.0.n: A shortened まあ, used to ease into the next point.

2.2.n: 間 marks a duration, so 2年間 describes a two-year period.

2.3.n: After 2年間, 限定 restricts the measure to that duration.

2.4.n: Links the content 2年間限定 to 見通し, explaining what the outlook is.

2.5.n: Refers to an expectation about how the measure will develop, rather than a guaranteed outcome.

2.6.n: Marks the outlook as the subject the speaker is addressing.

3.0.n: A hesitation filler here, not the word meaning that before a noun.

3.2.n: A neutral first-person pronoun, suitable for this formal statement.

3.3.n: After 私, 自身 emphasizes the speaker’s own position.

3.4.n: Marks 私自身 as the topic, focusing on the speaker personally.

3.5.n: A noun from 変わる, referring here to a change in the speaker’s position.

3.6.n: Highlights 変わり before the negative statement, emphasizing that there is no change.

3.7.n: The stem in ございません, a more formal and polite version of ありません.

3.8.n: This is the ませ portion of ません, the polite negative ending.

3.9.n: Completes ません; together, ございません politely states that no change exists.

0.lit: Well, as for the core goal, a tax credit with a payment, I have been saying.
0.tip: 申し上げてまいりました is a humble, formal way to say the speaker has been maintaining this position.

1.lit: Since I have been saying it is a stopgap until that situation can be achieved,
1.tip: までの links an endpoint to a noun: a stopgap lasting until the stated goal becomes achievable.

2.lit: Well, regarding the outlook that it is limited to two years,
2.tip: という introduces the content of 見通し: the expectation that the measure will last only two years.

3.lit: Um, as for myself, there is no change.
3.tip: 変わりはございません formally says there is no change; here, the unchanged thing is the speaker’s position.
